title: Delayed Cord Clamping in Very Low Birth Weight Infants
brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to determine if there is a difference in neonatal outcomes with delayed umbilical cord clamping at 30 versus 60 seconds. Our primary outcome will be intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) (bleeding in the brain) in these infants.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Pregnant women who are expected to deliver a very low birth weight infant
* Neonates born weighing \>= 500g and \<1500 grams
* Mother 18 years of age or older
* English speaking mother

Exclusion Criteria:

* Placental abruption
* Vasa previa
* Fetal hydrops or other signs of fetal volume overload
* Other major fetal anomalies
* Placenta Accreta
* Mother \< 18 years of age
* Non-English speaking mother
* Infants \>= 1500g (3.3 lbs) or \<500g
